issue.title: Cache agent-name registry during bead-page publication
issue.description: Post-completion commit tracking repeatedly rebuilds agent-name registry state for every bead association while publishing committed bead pages, causing sustained high CPU while holding the bead-store write lock. Recurrence observed after sase-bo; prior evidence was recorded as a proposed follow-up on sase-bj.1.

fields.description: Post-completion commit tracking calls publish_committed_bead_pages, where build_bead_association_index resolves each agent URL and repeatedly reloads/staleness-checks the agent-name registry via get_reserved_family_names. On the sase-bo finalizer this consumed about 86% CPU for more than four minutes while holding sase-store-write.lock; SIGINT showed the hot stack in _registry_source_signature_paths. The durable commit 9562e5366 was already pushed and the worktree synchronized. Cache or snapshot registry/family-name state once per publication build, add regression/performance coverage, and verify the commit wrapper exits promptly. This is a recurrence of the proposed follow-up on sase-bj.1.
